body:
When using a session manager and in the off-chance that there's a real souce file named 'Starter' in the session, restoring the session with this file from mini.starter causes an [issue](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/discussions/786)

This is because mini.starter buffer name conflicts with the real source file named Starter.

This can be avoided by using a scheme-like name for the starter buffer which is a common practice for buffers created by plugins.

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

comment_regular_data.body:
Thanks for the PR!

Would you mind answering the #787 first?
Sure thing, answered. And yes it works.

OK, thanks!

I quite like how "Starter" name is shown in statusline, while "starter://1" does not look too good (especially for new users). I'll take a moment to think if preserving current naming is important or not.

I think the PR i have here is a good compromise no? 

This is what other plugins do "[plugins]://[BufferName]" 

This pr has that format ^, FWIW.

Thanks again for the PR!

I decided to go a slightly more complicated route of trying to use current 'Starter_x' format as it is more user friendly to see in the statusline.

Cool. 

I have some autocommands written to sure my session plugin does not save a session if the current buffer is the starter buffer. 

It relies on finding "Starter" in the name, can i safely move this to looking for "starter://" string in buffername everytime?

> It relies on finding "Starter" in the name, can i safely move this to looking for "starter://" string in buffername everytime?

No, as 'mini.starter' still prefers "Starter" as the buffer name in most situations. The most reliable way to tell if the buffer is from 'mini.starter' is to check that it has 'starter' filetype. So like `vim.bo.filetype == 'starter'`.

Ah I see your solution there. 

Ugh, from a integration point of view, this is kinda bad. 

Plugins or scripts which want to look for the starter page now has to check both for plain "Starter" and "starter://" in buf name, and it means if Starter is a real file in the repo, matching becomes inconvenient :/

it would be really helpful to just stick to a scheme so users (especially with regard to session management) who write scripts against mini.starter can always identify the starter buffer 

Or maybe allow a user defined prefix/name?
> The most reliable way to tell if the buffer is from 'mini.starter' is to check that it has 'starter' filetype. So like `vim.bo.filetype == 'starter'`.
Yup i wrote that response before my ui updated with yours. Sounds good.

@ldelossa, just an FYI. Resolving #1455 indeed moved to a consistent naming for buffers that are created by modules. I still don't like the fact that statusline will not show `Starter` as buffer name (it is `ministarter://1/welcome` now), but that is the price for a consistent application of a general principle.

The `vim.bo.filetype == 'ministarter'` is still the most reliable way to identify the buffer created by 'mini.starter', though.

Awesome! While its a bit ugly, it seems to be the canonical way that plugins are moving too. Thanks for the heads up. Tho, i did think using the filetype to inform if a special buffer was adequate as well.
